findings.evidence: "The IT asset group updates the reimbursement log at the start of the fiscal year... Similarly, the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month."
findings.violation: The word "Similarly" is incorrect because these two processes occur on different schedules (fiscal year start vs. first business day of month), not in parallel.

findings.evidence: "The IT asset group updates the reimbursement log at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Either define what the reimbursement log contains and how it differs from the request log, or remove this reference if it is not relevant to the policy.
findings.violation: The term "reimbursement log" is never defined, explained, or mentioned anywhere else in the document.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Clarify: "Employees returning from approved leave retain their prior service time and do not need to restart the 90-day eligibility waiting period."
findings.violation: It is unclear whether employees returning from leave must complete a new 90-day waiting period or if their prior service time counts toward eligibility.

findings.evidence: "However, an incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives."
findings.fix: Change to: "However, an incomplete request pauses the timeline until the employee provides the missing information."
findings.violation: The phrase "missing item" is misleading; an incomplete request means missing documentation or information, not a physical missing item.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests... Additionally, employees must retain receipts for one year after the purchase date."
findings.fix: Clarify whether digital photos alone satisfy the requirement or if original receipts must also be kept on file, and for how long.
findings.violation: These statements are contradictory - if a photo is sufficient for submission, why must original receipts be retained for one year?

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Change to: "Employees must keep their equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This sentence switches to second person ("You," "we"), breaking the third-person voice used throughout the rest of the document.

findings.evidence: "The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year" vs. "the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Clarify the maximum number of items or categories permitted per benefit year, with examples if applicable.
findings.location: Eligibility and Restrictions and Exceptions sections
findings.violation: These two statements may contradict each other - it is unclear whether employees can claim one item per category or only one total claim per year.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form" (Terminology Notes) vs. "Employees start a stipend request in the benefits portal" (How to Apply).
findings.fix: Use consistent terminology throughout, or if both systems exist, explain their relationship and which one employees use.
findings.location: Terminology Notes and How to Apply sections
findings.violation: The document uses both "request form" and "benefits portal" without clarifying whether these refer to the same system or two different systems.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Either expand this section to fully detail all steps or remove it as redundant to How to Apply.
findings.violation: This description is vague and incomplete compared to the detailed How to Apply section, which includes portal navigation, automatic draft saving, and summary review before submission.

findings.evidence: "IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog" (Program Overview) vs. "The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog" (Special Cases) vs. "The benefits team reviews the equipment catalog" (Questions and Updates).
findings.fix: Consolidate all catalog management responsibility under one department and one update schedule, and remove conflicting references.
findings.location: Program Overview, Special Cases, and Questions and Updates sections
findings.violation: Three different departments are described as managing the equipment catalog, creating confusion about who holds this responsibility.

findings.evidence: "The manager reviews the request within two business days" (Approval Timeline) vs. "The team then routes the request to the correct approver based on department" (Program Coordination).
findings.fix: Clarify the approval chain: Is the manager always the first reviewer, and if so, is the manager also the final approver, or is there a secondary review step?
findings.location: Approval Timeline and Program Coordination sections
findings.violation: It is unclear whether the manager is the final approver or if requests are routed to different approvers depending on department.

findings.evidence: The entire section makes no mention of finance office review, while the Review Responsibility section states "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Add a step to Approval Timeline describing when and how the finance office review occurs in relation to manager approval and payment.
findings.violation: The Approval Timeline section describes an incomplete approval process, omitting the finance office review requirement for requests exceeding $200.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Simplify the language and define the term clearly: "Employees submit requests through the benefits portal. Finance reviews and reconciles all requests monthly, then Payroll releases reimbursement after this review."
findings.violation: The phrase "stipend item" is repeated three times in quick succession, making the section difficult to read, and the meaning of "stipend item" is never defined.
